# NEMAR

> The Neuroelectromagnetic Data Archive and Tools Resource: an open archive of human EEG, MEG,
> and iEEG datasets in Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) format, many with Hierarchical Event
> Descriptors (HED) and many sourced from OpenNeuro. Dataset pages are at nemar.org/dataset/<id>;
> the data itself is at data.nemar.org and is fetched with nemar-cli, not scraped from the page.

## Start here
- [Browse datasets](https://nemar.org): search and filter the archive; a dataset page is https://nemar.org/dataset/<id>
- [Documentation](https://docs.nemar.org): guides and the command-line reference
- [Data host](https://data.nemar.org): the actual BIDS dataset files, at /<id>/latest/

## Query the catalog without downloading
- `GET https://api.nemar.org/datasets`: the catalog
- `GET https://api.nemar.org/datasets/search`: search it
- `GET https://api.nemar.org/datasets/<id>`: one dataset's metadata, including its DOI and license

## Get the data
- [nemar-cli](https://github.com/nemarOrg/nemar-cli): `bun add -g nemar-cli` or `npm install -g nemar-cli`, then `nemar dataset download <id>` for the full dataset. `clone` alone does not fetch data; use `nemar dataset clone <id>` then `nemar dataset get <path>` for a selective download. `nemar dataset list`, `nemar dataset search <query>`, and `nemar dataset status <id>` (alias `view` from nemar-cli 0.9.15) answer most questions without downloading anything
- Direct file fetch: `wget https://data.nemar.org/<id>/latest/<file>` for small subsets
- [NSG compute](https://nemar.org/nsg_for_nemar): process datasets without downloading them

## Read a slice without downloading
- [Zarr serving copy](https://zarr.nemar.org): a derived, latest-only copy for remote reads. Start at `https://zarr.nemar.org/<id>/zarr/index.json`, the mandatory entry point, and read `contract_base`, `data_base`, and `s3_uri` from it rather than hardcoding a bucket path
- Stream for a slice of channels, time, or subjects; download the BIDS tree when you will touch most of the array
- `HEAD` is never redirected; a plain `GET` from a non-browser client is redirected to the public S3 object, so follow redirects. Only `index.json` is always proxied; the sibling `manifest.json` and `events.parquet` redirect like store objects

## Understand the data
- [BIDS](https://bids.neuroimaging.io): how each dataset is structured
- [HED](https://www.hedtags.org): the event annotations
- [OpenNeuro](https://openneuro.org): the upstream source of many datasets

## Notes for agents
- A dataset page carries server-rendered schema.org `Dataset` JSON-LD with the DOI, the license,
  and the distribution URLs. Read that first; the files themselves are not in the HTML.
- DOIs are minted through EZID and DataCite as `10.82901/nemar.<id>`,
  so the DOI resolves and negotiates to a full metadata record on its own.
- Dataset licenses vary and are often non-commercial. Check each dataset's license before use.
